row.evidence: Rippling's pricing page says each HR, Finance and IT product "can be purchased separately—alongside the core, required Rippling Platform" on a custom quote, and its Identity & Access Management product provides "provisioning with JIT or SCIM" to connected apps.
row.notes: Recorded as in June: Rippling is an HRIS and identity provider, so this row records Rippling's own SCIM provisioning (Rippling as SCIM client pushing users to other apps through the Identity & Access Management product), like the Okta row. Rippling documents no inbound SCIM endpoint for provisioning users into Rippling; its users come from its own HR records, and the v2 REST API exposes users read-only. Status unchanged (gated): IAM is an IT product bought separately on top of the required Rippling Platform, price by custom quote only. June's '~$8/u/mo IAM module', '~$8/u/mo + $35/mo platform fee' and '$2,000 implementation fee' figures have no first-party source and are dropped. scim_ops and IdP fields are null because they describe inbound SCIM, which Rippling does not document. Help centre (help.rippling.com) search pages could not be loaded.

plans.name: Rippling Platform (core, required)
plans.notes: Products are billed mostly per employee per month, some with a monthly base fee; no public prices.

plans.name: Identity & Access Management (IT product, purchased separately)
plans.notes: SSO and SCIM here are Rippling acting as the IdP for other apps.

scim.notes: Rippling acts as the SCIM client (outbound provisioning to 600+ apps and custom SCIM apps). No inbound SCIM endpoint into Rippling is documented.

operations.notes: Outbound: create or suspend app access by rules, deprovision on offboarding, group access driven by Supergroups.

deprovision.notes: Outbound behaviour in downstream apps; depends on each app's integration.

custom.how: Custom attribute mapping; 'hundreds of user attributes' beyond standard SCIM attributes.

limitations.text: No inbound SCIM endpoint is documented for creating users in Rippling; Rippling is the source of truth.

auth.notes: Bearer API tokens inherit the creator's permission profile; App Shop partner apps use OAuth 2.0. Tokens are revoked if unused for 30 days.

capabilities.notes: v2 Users endpoints are read-only; new people enter through draft hires (POST bulk draft hire) and HR approval. Supergroup inclusion/exclusion members can be updated.

endpoints.purpose: List users (accounts that can sign in, with access/roles/app provisioning info)

webhooks_user_events.notes: Webhooks are documented as triggers into Rippling Workflows (c22), not outbound user-event webhooks.

rate_limits.text: Burst threshold of 300 requests per IP per 10-second window; page size default 50, max 100.

entra.notes: No Entra rippling-tutorial or rippling-provisioning-tutorial page (404).

fallbacks.other_sync: Rippling is the HR source of truth; users are created from Rippling HR records (draft hires).

Which Rippling plan or product lets customers sign in to Rippling with their own external IdP (SAML) is not documented in pages I could load.
